title: Charles Darwin University RTP Scholarship 2026/27: Research Funding for PhD and Master by Research Students in Australia
summary: Charles Darwin University (CDU) offers Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) Scholarships to high-performing Higher Degree by Research candidates undertaking a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or Master by Research in Australia. The RTP is one of Australia’s principal funding mechanisms for postgraduate research. At Charles Darwin University, scholarships are awarded competitively to candidates who demonstrate strong academic performance, substantial research preparation, high-quality research outputs or research experience, and alignment with CDU’s research priorities. Both domestic and international candidates can meet the general RTP eligibility framework, although the availability of scholarships differs substantially between the two groups and between specific research projects. For 2026, CDU lists an RTP stipend of: AUD $35,489 per year for full-time students, tax-free and paid fortnightly. For part-time recipients, the published 2026 rate is: AUD $17,744.50 per year, taxable and paid fortnightly. CDU states that stipend support normally runs for three years for a doctoral degree and two years for a research Master’s degree . Additional benefits can include paid sick leave, maternity leave and a relocation allowance of up to AUD $2,000 for domestic recipients and AUD $2,500 for international recipients , subject to conditions. However, prospective applicants should pay close attention to an important update before relying on social-media posts advertising a general “2027 RTP Scholarship” with a 30 September 2026 deadline . Important Application Status Update The current official CDU information does not support advertising the RTP as a general open application round with a confirmed 30 September 2026 closing date. CDU’s current RTP information page states that: Research Training Program Scholarships are by invitation only. Applicants must first be invited by the CDU Higher Degree by Research team before they can submit the formal RTP scholarship application. In addition, CDU’s current project-focused scholarship information indicates that scholarship opportunities for 2026/27 are attached to pre-approved research projects and primarily target new HDR candidates . The university’s most recent international scholarship information says the International PhD RTP Scholarship is closed and that no international RTP scholarships remain for Semester 1, 2027, while future opportunities may be announced later. Therefore, the frequently circulated statement that the “Charles Darwin University RTP Scholarship 2027 is open to all nationalities until 30 September 2026” should not currently be presented as an official CDU deadline . Applicants should instead follow the live CDU scholarship pages and, where applicable, the instructions associated with a specific research project. Official CDU RTP information About the Australian Government Research Training Program The Research Training Program is funded by the Australian Government and administered through eligible Australian universities. Rather than students applying directly to the Australian Government, the government provides funding to participating higher education providers, and each university manages its own: Scholarship application system Eligibility process Ranking process Selection process Scholarship conditions The Australian Government confirms that RTP funding supports both domestic and overseas students undertaking research doctorates and research Master’s degrees at eligible Australian higher education institutions. RTP support can take three broad forms: Tuition fee offsets Stipends for general living expenses Allowances associated with the additional costs of undertaking higher-degree research At Charles Darwin University, which forms of support a candidate receives can depend on their scholarship type, citizenship status and the particular research opportunity. What Degrees Are Eligible at Charles Darwin University? For RTP purposes, CDU defines Higher Degree by Research programmes as: Doctor of Philosophy and: Master by Research The scholarship is therefore not intended for ordinary coursework degrees such as: Taught Master’s programmes Graduate certificates Graduate diplomas Undergraduate programmes CDU’s current eligibility guidelines explicitly state that the relevant HDR programmes are the Doctor of Philosophy and Master by Research . Charles Darwin University PhD Opportunities CDU is currently promoting a project-focused scholarship model for 2026/27. The university lists pre-approved HDR projects across strategic research fields and allows new applicants to submit expressions of interest directly to relevant project supervisors. Research areas represented across CDU projects include subjects such as: Indigenous studies Ecology Remote health Energy Artificial intelligence Sustainability Specific eligibility and scholarship availability can differ by project, so candidates should not assume that every PhD project automatically includes the same funding package. Current Domestic Scholarship Opportunities For domestic candidates, CDU currently lists opportunities including the: RTP Domestic PhD Scholarship which provides approximately the standard CDU RTP stipend together with an RTP fee offset covering PhD tuition fees for up to three years. CDU also lists a: DVCRCC Domestic Strategic Project Scholarship which may combine the standard RTP stipend with an additional top-up of up to approximately AUD $18,000 per year , together with a full fee offset for up to three years. These project-specific opportunities demonstrate why applicants should review the actual project listing rather than assuming that every CDU research scholarship has identical financial conditions. Current International Scholarship Position International candidates need to exercise particular caution. The general RTP framework does permit international applicants, and CDU’s eligibility rules explicitly state that both domestic and international students can be eligible for consideration. However, that does not mean that unrestricted international RTP places are always available. CDU’s current project-focused scholarship page states that the International PhD RTP Scholarship for international applicants is highly limited, while the most recent scholarship listing indicates that it is closed and not accepting applications , with no international RTP scholarships currently left for Semester 1, 2027. CDU does separately advertise Graduate Full Fee Scholarships for selected international HDR applicants, covering tuition fees for eligible research programmes. International applicants should therefore distinguish carefully between: RTP stipend funding Tuition-only scholarships Project-specific scholarships Other international research scholarships A tuition waiver alone is not the same as receiving an RTP living stipend. How Much Is the CDU RTP Stipend? CDU currently publishes the 2026 stipend rate as: Full-Time Students AUD $35,489 per year The stipend is: Tax-free Paid in fortnightly instalments Part-Time Students AUD $17,744.50 per year The part-time stipend is: Taxable Paid fortnightly These are CDU’s stated 2026 rates. Applicants should not automatically describe AUD $35,489 as the confirmed 2027 CDU stipend unless CDU publishes that figure for 2027. The Australian Government separately establishes indexed RTP base and maximum stipend rates nationally each year. For 2027, the federal minimum full-time RTP stipend rate is listed as AUD $35,550 , but universities can set their institutional scholarship rate within the permitted range. CDU applicants should therefore use the university’s own rate once its 2027 amount is formally published. How Long Does RTP Funding Last? CDU’s current scholarship information states that stipend funding normally runs for: Three years full-time for a doctoral degree and: Two years for a research Master’s degree. The broader Australian Government framework allows universities some flexibility over doctoral RTP support periods, but university-specific scholarship conditions ultimately determine the individual recipient’s funded period. Candidates should therefore read the CDU scholarship offer and conditions carefully if selected. Tuition Fee Support Tuition arrangements differ between domestic and international research candidates. Domestic RTP Fee Offset Domestic RTP recipients can receive a: Full RTP fee offset which covers eligible research degree tuition costs for the standard funded period. For project-based domestic PhD scholarships, CDU states that the fee offset can cover PhD tuition fees for up to three years. International Tuition Fee Support For international candidates, tuition support is more limited and competitive. CDU indicates that international applicants awarded an RTP stipend may receive a Graduate Full Fee Scholarship covering international Higher Degree by Research tuition fees for the normal degree period. CDU’s course information explains that these international tuition fee waivers are limited and normally cover: Three years full-time for a PhD Two years full-time for a Master by Research International candidates who do not receive a fee-waiver scholarship may instead receive an offer as a full fee-paying research student. For this reason, describing the CDU RTP as automatically covering tuition for every international candidate would be inaccurate. Relocation Allowance CDU also identifies relocation support as one of the possible RTP benefits. The current published maximum allowance is: Up to AUD $2,000 for domestic students and: Up to AUD $2,500 for international students subject to applicable conditions. Candidates should review the scholarship terms to determine: Eligible relocation expenses Documentation required Claim deadlines Whether reimbursement or another payment method applies Paid Leave Benefits Additional benefits listed by CDU include: Paid sick leave Maternity leave The precise conditions and entitlements depend on the scholarship rules. Candidates with family, medical or caregiving considerations should consult CDU’s RTP conditions rather than assuming ordinary employment leave rules apply. Who Can Be Considered for the CDU RTP Scholarship? The current CDU RTP eligibility framework requires candidates to satisfy five broad conditions. Applicants must: Be a domestic or international candidate. Meet CDU academic and English-language admission requirements. Be invited to apply by the CDU HDR team. Submit a complete RTP scholarship application by the deadline communicated to them. Not receive equivalent financial support from another source for their HDR studies. The third requirement is particularly important: The formal RTP application is invitation-only. A prospective student therefore cannot necessarily submit an unrestricted scholarship application simply because they meet the academic criteria. What Counts as a Domestic Student? CDU defines domestic students as: Australian citizens Australian permanent residents New Zealand citizens Other applicants are generally categorized as international students. Academic Requirements for a Master by Research For scholarship ranking, Master by Research applicants are expected to demonstrate relevant research training. CDU states that applicants should have completed at least: Half a semester full-time equivalent or: 20 credit points of research activity at AQF Level 8 or above within a relevant qualification. The university assesses both: Academic performance Quality and amount of previous research preparation Academic Requirements for PhD Applicants PhD applicants need stronger prior research preparation. CDU states that candidates should have completed at least: One semester full-time equivalent or: 40 credit points of research activity at AQF Level 8 or above. Relevant evidence can include: Research thesis Dissertation Research units Honours research Master’s research components Applicants must clearly identify which parts of previous degrees involved research and how heavily those units were weighted. General HDR Entry Standard For project-focused PhD opportunities, CDU summarizes its HDR academic expectation as a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree with a: Distinction-level GPA together with appropriate research preparation. If a candidate does not meet the research-unit requirement exactly, CDU may consider equivalent research experience where the applicant can demonstrate a sufficiently strong research record. This flexibility is especially relevant to candidates whose home universities use different programme structures. International English-Language Requirements International applicants must also satisfy CDU’s English requirements. For the current project scholarship campaign, CDU provides an example of: IELTS 6.5 overall, with no individual band below 6.0 and also notes acceptance of the: Duolingo English Test and other approved tests. Applicants should check the requirements for their specific HDR programme because accepted tests and exemptions can vary. Scholarship Selection Is Highly Competitive Meeting the minimum admission conditions does not mean that an applicant will receive an RTP scholarship. CDU states clearly that: Australian Government RTP Stipend Scholarships are awarded to students of exceptional research potential and are not automatically granted to all HDR students. Scholarship applications are ranked competitively. CDU currently evaluates applicants across four broad areas: Qualifications and academic performance Quality research publications and non-traditional research outputs Research experience or portfolio Alignment with strategic research priorities Academic Performance Academic results form an important part of the ranking process. CDU expects applicants to demonstrate: Strong GPA Relevant Bachelor’s, Honours or Master’s qualifications Adequate research training Strong thesis or dissertation performance International applicants must make their grading systems understandable to CDU. This may require submitting: Official transcripts Grading scale explanations Course or unit outlines Thesis information Official English translations Research Publications Research outputs can significantly strengthen an RTP application. CDU says successful candidates will typically demonstrate recent, high-quality: Peer-reviewed research publications as either: First author Co-author The university can also consider eligible: Non-Traditional Research Outputs such as creative or discipline-specific research products where appropriate. Candidates may submit up to four primary outputs demonstrating their research quality, impact and relevance. Quality Matters More Than Quantity CDU explicitly advises candidates to focus on: Quality over quantity. Listing a large number of publications without evidence of their quality will not necessarily make an application stronger. Applicants should therefore identify their strongest work and provide evidence such as: DOI Journal ranking Peer-review status Publisher information Publication details Research impact Publications Must Be Formally Accepted CDU does not treat all unpublished manuscripts equally. Outputs must generally be: Published In press Formally accepted after peer review Manuscripts that are merely: Submitted Under review In revision are not assessed as completed research outputs for scholarship ranking. This distinction is especially important for early-career researchers preparing an application close to the scholarship assessment period. Research Experience Applicants may also receive credit for broader research experience not already captured by academic qualifications or publications. Relevant experience can include: Research employment Work at a reputable university Research institute employment Research-related professional work Other recognised research outputs Substantial research portfolio CDU requires claims to be supported with clear documentation. Strategic Research Alignment CDU may give additional weight to research proposals that align with: University strategic research priorities Institutional research strengths Existing research capabilities This makes supervisor and project fit especially important. An academically excellent applicant proposing work unrelated to available expertise may be less competitive than a candidate whose research fits strongly within an established CDU team. What Does a Strong Applicant Look Like? CDU’s current project scholarship guidance says strong applicants will generally have a combination of: Excellent academic record Honours or Master’s research training High GPA Research publications Practical research experience Skills aligned with the project The university notes that highly competitive applicants typically have at least one strong publication, such as a quality journal article, or a Master by Research/MPhil with a GPA of around 80% or higher . This is indicative of competitiveness rather than a universal minimum requirement for every project. How the Current Application Process Works The current CDU process is not simply: “Fill out an RTP scholarship form before September 30.” For project-focused opportunities, applicants generally begin with an: Expression of Interest to the lead supervisor. The EOI should include: A cover email explaining PhD eligibility, suitability for the research project and motivation Curriculum vitae Relevant qualifications and research experience Up to four strong publications where possible Postgraduate transcripts Grading system information Evidence of thesis or research components Key Details at a Glance University: Charles Darwin University Country: Australia Funding programme: Australian Government Research Training Program Study level: Higher Degree by Research Eligible degrees: Doctor of Philosophy and Master by Research CDU full-time stipend: AUD $35,489 per year at the published 2026 rate Part-time stipend: AUD $17,744.50 per year at the published 2026 rate Payment: Fortnightly Full-time stipend tax status: Tax-free Doctoral stipend duration: Normally three years at CDU Master by Research duration: Normally two years Relocation allowance: Up to AUD $2,000 domestic / AUD $2,500 international, subject to conditions Other benefits: Paid sick leave and maternity leave Domestic eligibility: Australian citizens, Australian permanent residents and New Zealand citizens International eligibility: International applicants can meet general RTP eligibility, subject to scholarship availability Formal scholarship application: By invitation only Current international 2027 status: International RTP availability is extremely limited; CDU’s latest public information indicates no general international Semester 1, 2027 RTP places remain Tips for Prospective Applicants 1. Find a Suitable Research Project First CDU’s current scholarship model strongly emphasizes pre-approved projects. Start by identifying: Research topic Faculty Supervisor Project fit before worrying about the formal RTP application. 2. Contact the Lead Supervisor A strong initial email should explain: Your research background Why you meet CDU PhD or Master by Research admission requirements Why you fit the project Your strongest research achievements Why you want to work with that supervisor Avoid generic mass emails. 3. Make Your Research Training Easy to Assess International degree structures can differ significantly from Australia’s. Clearly show: Which courses were research-based Credit weighting Thesis length Thesis grade Research methodology training CDU states that it is the applicant’s responsibility to make this information clear. 4. Provide Your Strongest Research Outputs If you have publications, prioritize the strongest four. Explain: Journal quality Peer review DOI Your contribution Relevance to the proposed research 5. Do Not Assume Admission Equals Scholarship An applicant may be academically eligible for a PhD but not competitive enough for RTP funding. Scholarship selection is substantially more competitive than minimum programme admission. 6. International Applicants Should Check Availability Before Spending Time on a Full Application This is especially important for 2027. CDU’s current information indicates very limited or closed international RTP availability for Semester 1, 2027. Contact the relevant supervisor or CDU HDR team before preparing a large application package. Conclusion The Charles Darwin University Research Training Program Scholarship remains an attractive Australian postgraduate research funding pathway for highly competitive candidates pursuing a PhD or Master by Research . CDU’s published 2026 full-time RTP stipend is AUD $35,489 per year , paid fortnightly and tax-free. Part-time recipients receive AUD $17,744.50 annually, taxable. Scholarship benefits can also include tuition support, paid leave and relocation assistance. The scholarship is competitive rather than automatic. Applicants are ranked according to factors including academic performance, research preparation, publications, broader research experience and alignment with CDU research priorities. Importantly, CDU’s current system requires candidates to be invited by the HDR team before submitting a formal RTP application . Please visit RTP Scholarship Ranking Guidelines before applying.
